summary: 面部表情究竟多大程度能揭示真实感受？研究者比较表情与情绪的对应关系，以及表情调节社会互动的作用；他们也指出，要判断一个人接下来的行动，还须观察语气、姿势和情境。
logic: 表情与情绪的传统研究
独处时也可能想象他人

paragraphs.brief: 使用面部表情来测量人们的情绪自20世纪60年代后期以来一直以心理学为主导
sentences: The use of facial expressions for measuring people’s emotions has dominated psychology since the late 1960s.
使用面部表情来测量人们的情绪自20世纪60年代后期以来一直以心理学为主导
This was when Paul Ekman of the University of California pioneered the idea that, by carefully measuring facial expression, he could evaluate people’s true emotions.
加州大学的保罗·艾克曼率先提出这样的想法，即通过仔细测量面部表情，他可以评估人们的真实情绪。
Ekman carried out experiments in which people were asked to label photos of basic facial expressions - such as a smile, frown or scowl - with words for emotions.
Ekman进行了一些实验，要求人们用情感语言标注基本面部表情的照片，如微笑、皱眉或皱眉。
He found, for example, that a smile represented joy and a scowl represented anger.
例如，他发现笑容代表喜悦，而肉肉代表愤怒。

In fact, since the 1970s Ekman has dominated the field of emotion research with his theory that when an emotion occurs, a large number of electrical impulses also occur, creating specific facial expressions and other physiological changes, such as increased or decreased heart rate or heightened blood pressure.
事实上，自1970年代以来，Ekman一直主导情感研究领域，他理论认为，当情绪发生时，也会出现大量的电脉冲，造成特定的面部表情和其他生理变化，如心率上升或下降或血压升高。

paragraphs.brief: 许多人认为Ekman的作品暗示面部表情准确地表明了人们的感受。
sentences: Many took Ekman’s work to imply that facial expressions precisely indicated people’s feelings.
许多人认为Ekman的作品暗示面部表情准确地表明了人们的感受。

However, this theory has been attacked by a number of psychologists, such as Alan Fridlund of the University of California, who claim that there is no one-to-one correspondence between facial expressions and emotions.
然而，这一理论受到一些心理学家的攻击，例如加利福尼亚大学的Alan Fridlund，他声称面部表情和情绪之间没有一对一的对应关系。
Expressions evolved to set off certain behaviors in other people, says Fridlund.
Fridlund说，表达方式的进化激发了其他人的某些行为。
So a smile may prompt people to approach, a scowl may warn them to stay away, and a look of sadness may elicit words of sympathy and reassurance.
微笑可能会促使人们接近，斯考普可能会警告他们远离，悲伤的表情可能会引起同情和安慰的言词。
In other words, in Fridlund’s view, facial expressions are inherently social - they involve not one, but two or more people.
换句话说，Fridlund认为，面部表情本质上是社交性的，它们涉及的不是一个人，而是两个或两个以上的人。
Even when people are alone they are holding a dialog with another person internally, or imagining themselves in a social situation.
即使在人们孤独的时候，他们也与另一个人在国内进行对话，或想象自己处于一种社会状况。

paragraphs.brief: 在这些关键点上，有一种方法，或近距离，或更亲近，面部表情，以及手势，为各种社会互动提供了可能性。
sentences: Thus Fridlund thinks of facial expressions as tools for influencing social interactions, a view which, he claims, enables us to begin predicting when certain facial expressions will occur.
因此，Fridlund认为面部表情是影响社会互动的工具，他声称，这种观点使我们能够开始预测何时会出现某些面部表态。
This in turn will allow more precise theories about social interactions.
这反过来又将使人们能够对社会互动有更精确的理论。
His studies find that expressions occur most often during pivotal points, the turning points in social interactions - during greetings, social crises, or times of appeasement, for example.
他的研究发现，表达最常发生在关键点、社会互动的转折点 -- -- 例如，在问候、社会危机或安抚时期。
At these pivotal points there is an approach, or closeness, or more intimacy, and facial expressions, as well as gestures, open up the possibilities of various social interactions.
在这些关键点上，有一种方法，或近距离，或更亲近，面部表情，以及手势，为各种社会互动提供了可能性。

paragraphs.brief: 不列颠哥伦比亚大学说很少有证据可以证明这种联系：“虽然很多关于情绪的工作都依赖于面部表情和情绪之间的联系心理学家詹姆斯・罗素。”
sentences: Although much work on the emotions relies on a link between facial expression and emotions, psychologist James Russell, of the University of British Columbia, says there is very little evidence supporting such a connection.
不列颠哥伦比亚大学说很少有证据可以证明这种联系：“虽然很多关于情绪的工作都依赖于面部表情和情绪之间的联系心理学家詹姆斯・罗素。”
‘There’s some sense in which faces express emotion, but only in the sense that everything expresses emotion,’ says Russell, a long-time critic of the expression-emotion link.
Russell说长期批评表达 -情感联系的人：“有某种感觉面部表达情感但只有感官什么都表达情感。”
‘Music does, posture does, words do, tone of voice does, your behavior does.
音乐姿势语言声音行为
The real question is, “Is there anything special about faces?”
真正的问题是，“面孔有什么特别之处吗？”
And there we really do not know much.
在那里，我们真的不知道多少。
What is more likely, argues Russell, is that facial expressions tell others something about a person’s overall mood and context, rather than provide details about specific emotions.’
Russell认为，更可能的情况是脸部表情告诉别人一个人的总体情绪和背景，而不是提供具体情绪的细节。

paragraphs.brief: 有时面部表情出现时没有相应的情绪
sentences: Others, including Ekman, argue that the face can display information about emotions, but they admit that it is not reliable one hundred percent of the time.
包括Ekman在内的其他人则认为，脸部可以显示情感信息，但他们承认，百分之百的时间都不可靠。
And those who only examine faces when trying to study emotion will jump to false conclusions.
那些在试图研究情感时只检查面孔的人将会跳到错误的结论。
But according to Ekman, to say, as Fridlund does, that there is no connection at all between facial expressions and emotions is simply wrong.
但根据Ekman的说法，就像Fridlund一样，面部表情和情感之间没有任何联系，完全是错的。
‘There is a link between facial expression and emotion,’ agrees developmental psychologist Linda Camras of DePaul University, ‘but it’s not a one-to-one kind of relationship as many once thought.’
“面部表情和情感之间有联系，”同意德保罗大学发展心理学家Linda Camras的看法，“但不像许多人曾经想的那样是一对一的关系。
She believes there are many situations where emotion is experienced, yet no basic facial expression is displayed.
她认为有很多情况下情绪被体验过，但没有显示基本面部表情。
And there are times when a facial expression appears with no corresponding emotion.
有时面部表情出现时没有相应的情绪

paragraphs.brief: Ekman的理论指出，如果情绪慢慢地发作或相当弱，那么这种感觉可能不足以引发这种表达。
sentences: Ekman’s theory states that if the emotion comes on slowly or is rather weak, the feeling might not be strong enough to trigger the expression.
Ekman的理论指出，如果情绪慢慢地发作或相当弱，那么这种感觉可能不足以引发这种表达。
This would explain why there can sometimes be emotion without expression, he argues.
他争辩说，这可以解释为什么有时情绪不表露。
In addition, cultural rules - which determine when and whether people of certain cultures display emotional expressions - can prevent this otherwise automatic process from being completed.
此外，确定某些文化的人何时和是否表现出情感表达方式的文化规则可以阻止这种自动过程的完成。
Facial expressions evolved in humans as signals to others about how they feel, says Ekman.
埃克曼说：“人类的面部表达方式向他人发出信号说明他们的感受。”
At times, though, it may be uncomfortable or inconvenient for us to let others know our emotions.
有时，我们让别人知道我们的情绪可能不舒服或不方便。
But in the long run, over the course of evolution, it was useful to us as signalers: an angry look on someone’s face may be a warning that they are preparing to behave in an angry fashion.
但从长远看，在进化过程中，这对我们作为信号者很有用：对某人的脸部的愤怒表情可能是一种警告，警告他们准备以愤怒的方式行事。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然Fridlund在某些问题上不同意Ekman的观点，但两人基本同意面部表情表明人们未来的行动。
sentences: Although Fridlund disagrees with Ekman on certain matters, the two basically share the opinion that facial expressions indicate people’s future actions.
虽然Fridlund在某些问题上不同意Ekman的观点，但两人基本同意面部表情表明人们未来的行动。
The area of dispute between Fridlund and Ekman draws attention away from their major areas of agreement, says Joseph Campos of the University of California.
加州大学的Joseph Campos说：“Fridlund和Ekman之间的争端引起人们的注意，而忽略了它们的主要协议领域。”
Indeed, he says, ‘there is profound agreement that the face, along with the voice, body posture and hand gestures, forecasts to outside observers what people will do next.’
他说，“人们深刻地一致认为，脸部，连同声音、身体姿势和手势，都向外部观察家预测人们下一步会做什么。”

He goes on to say, ‘The face is a component [of emotion], but to make it the center of study of the human being experiencing an emotion is like saying the only thing you need to study in a car is the transmission.
他接着说，“面部是情感的一部分，但要使脸部成为人们体验情感的研究中心，就像说，在汽车里，你唯一需要学习的就是传输。
Not that the transmission is unimportant, but it’s only part of an entire system.’
不是说传输不重要而是整个系统的一部分"

items.en: a recognition that facial expressions do not always provide a true guide to feelings
items.zh: 面部表情并不总能真正指引感情
items.why: 这段话直接指出“并非百分之百可靠”““并非一一对应”,而且给出“有情无表/有表无情” 的两种情形，恰答“并不总能真实指引感受”。

items.en: examples of ways that a person’s facial expression can affect someone else’s actions
items.zh: 一个人的面部表情如何影响他人行为的例子
items.why: 题干要“影响他人行动的例子”,本段给出靠近/ 远离/表达安慰等具体行为，完全对应。

items.en: a reference to reasons for hiding emotions
items.why: 让别人知道真实感受有时会带来不适或不便，这给出了人们隐藏情绪的理由。

items.en: examples of times when facial expressions are used especially frequently
items.zh: 面部表达式使用时间的例子
items.why: 明确罗列“问候/社会危机/安抚时刻” 等“高频” 时间点。

items.en: examples of changes inside the body when an emotion is felt
items.zh: 感觉情绪时身体内变化的例子
items.why: 题干问“体内变化的例子”,本段给出心率增减、血压升高等生理例子。

items.en: Focusing on the face in researching emotions is similar to researching a large structure by looking at just one small unit of it.
items.zh: 关注面部研究情绪与研究大结构相似通过只看它的一个小单位。

items.en: Facial expressions developed in order to encourage other people to react in particular ways.
items.zh: 形成面部表达法是为了鼓励其他人采取特定方式作出反应。

items.en: Although certain researchers have different opinions about various points, they share some important ideas.
items.zh: 虽然某些研究人员对各种观点有不同的看法，但他们也有一些重要的想法。

items.en: Both emotion and expression can exist independently of each other in certain circumstances.
items.zh: 在某些情况下，情感和表达可以独立存在。

items.en: It cannot be proved that there is a connection between facial expression and real emotion.
items.zh: 不能证明面部表情和真实情感之间有联系。

items.en: In Fridlund’s view ________ on someone’s face may be intended as an invitation to come nearer.
items.zh: 弗里德隆德认为，一个人脸上的________可能是在邀请对方靠近。
items.why: 回到对应内容“微笑可能会促使人们接近，斯考普可能会警告他们远离，悲伤的表情可能会引起同情和安慰的言词”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: According to Fridlund, when we are by ourselves we still use facial expressions because we are having a ________ with someone in our minds.
items.zh: 据弗里德隆德解释，我们独处时仍有面部表情，是因为我们在心里与某人进行着________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“即使在人们孤独的时候，他们也与另一个人在国内进行对话，或想象自己处于一种社会状况”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Fridlund considers facial expressions to be ________ that can affect our contact with other people.
items.zh: 弗里德隆德把面部表情视为能够影响我们与他人交往的________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“因此，Fridlund认为面部表情是影响社会互动的工具，他声称，这种观点使我们能够开始预测何时会出现某些面部表态”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 让别人知道真实感受有时会带来不适或不便，这给出了人们隐藏情绪的理由。
回到对应内容“微笑可能会促使人们接近，斯考普可能会警告他们远离，悲伤的表情可能会引起同情和安慰的言词”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: “that a smile represented joy and a scowl represented anger”补足 found 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 found 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
Thus Fridlund thinks of facial expressions as tools for influencing social interactions, a view ….
“which, he claims, enables us to begin predicting when certain facial expressions will occur”修饰前面的 view。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 view，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Do facial expressions reflect inner feelings?
面部表情能反映内心的感受吗？
Or are they social devices for influencing others?
或者是用来影响他人的社交工具？
